requirements.quote:
Connection migration (Section 9) provides endpoints with the ability
   to transition between IP addresses and ports on multiple paths, using
   one path at a time for transmission and receipt of non-probing
   frames.  Path validation (Section 8.2) establishes that a peer is
   both willing and able to receive packets sent on a particular path.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint uses connection migration across multiple paths to transmit or receive non-probing frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Use only one path at a time for transmission and receipt of non-probing frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not simultaneously use multiple paths for transmission or receipt of non-probing frames.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can migrate a connection across multiple paths and observe whether non-probing frames are transmitted or accepted on more than one path at the same time.

requirements.quote:
frames.  Path validation (Section 8.2) establishes that a peer is
   both willing and able to receive packets sent on a particular path.
requirements.condition: When path validation succeeds for a particular path.
requirements.required_behavior: The validation must establish that the peer is both willing and able to receive packets on that path.
requirements.why_checkable: A path-validation test can verify that success is not recorded without peer behavior demonstrating receipt capability and willingness on the validated path.

requirements.quote:
This helps reduce the effects of address spoofing by limiting the
   number of packets sent to a spoofed address.
requirements.condition: When packets might be directed to a spoofed address.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the number of packets sent to the spoofed address.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage identifies packet limiting as the intended mitigation, but supplies no quantitative limit or precise trigger, so a conformance test cannot determine an exact pass condition from this chunk alone.
